title: Cap. V Obj. 6: without foresight faith Christ is shut out of the election decree
latin: Obj. 6. Si electio non sit ex fide praevisa, tum Christus excluditur a decreto electionis, et homines sunt prius praedestinati ut serventur, quam Christus ut eos servet; nam qui nondum credunt, sunt adhuc extra Christum: Christus autem praedestinatus est Salvator fidelium solummodo, et sibi per fidem conjunctorum: Ergo praedestinatio est ex fide praevisa, aut Christus (quod nefas est) a decreto electionis excludetur.
pass_a: Objection 6. If election is not from foresight faith, then Christ is shut out from the decree of election, and men are first predestinated that they may be saved, before Christ that he may save them; for those who do not yet believe are still outside Christ: But Christ has been predestinated Savior of the faithful only, and of those joined to himself by faith: Therefore predestination is from foresight faith, or Christ (which is impious) will be shut out from the decree of election.
pass_b: Obj. 6. If election is not from foresight faith, then Christ is shut out of the election decree, and men are predestinated to be saved before Christ is predestinated to save them — for those who do not yet believe are still outside Christ. But Christ was predestinated Savior only of the faithful, joined to him by faith. Therefore predestination is from foresight faith, or Christ (which is impious) is shut out of the election decree.

lemmas.gloss: Christ shut out of election decree

title: Cap. V Obj. 6 Sol: Major's consequence wobbles — elect in Christ as members to be united
latin: Sol. Vacillat Majoris consequentia. Nam quamvis decretum electionis tendat in hominem mortuum ac in massa perditionis jacentem, ita tamen tendit, ut vitam ei non decernat nisi quatenus consideratur ut membrum, juxta Divinae voluntatis beneplacitum, Christo uniendum, et per Christum vivificandum. Atque hoc sensu, in Christo eliguntur qui nondum per fidem in Christum insiti considerantur.
pass_a: Solution. The consequence of the Major wobbles. For although the decree of election tends upon a dead man and one lying in the mass of perdition, yet it so tends that it does not decree life to him except insofar as he is considered as a member, according to the good pleasure of the Divine will, to be united to Christ, and to be made alive through Christ. And in this sense, those are elected in Christ who are not yet considered grafted into Christ by faith.
pass_b: Sol. The Major's consequence wobbles. The election decree does tend on a dead man lying in the mass of perdition — yet so that it decrees him life only as considered a member, by God's good pleasure, to be united to Christ and made alive through Christ. In that sense they are elected in Christ who are not yet considered grafted into Christ by faith.

lemmas.gloss: to be united and made alive in Christ

title: Cap. V Obj. 6 Sol: Christ Head has causal priority — even the destined grafting comes from him
latin: Nam Caput Ecclesiae Christus ita conjunctus est cum membris suis omnibus, ut ipse prioritatem Causalitatis respectu reliquorum omnium obtineat, atque ut per et propter ipsum omnis boni gratuiti effluxus ad alios derivetur: derivatur autem non solummodo postquam sunt Christo insiti per fidem, sed ita ut hoc ipsum beneficium, quod per fidem illi inserendi destinantur, ab eo arcessendum sit, et in eo nobis conferendum. Quod igitur dicunt, Christum praedestinatum esse Salvatorem fidelium solummodo, id quidem verum est, quia non nisi per fidem omnes praedestinatos ad salutem perducit; non autem quia fides in omnibus praedestinatis ante ipsum decretum electionis invenitur.
pass_a: For Christ the Head of the Church is so joined with all his members, that he himself obtains the priority of Causality with respect to all the rest, and that through and on account of him every outflow of free good is derived to others: but it is derived not only after they have been grafted into Christ by faith, but so that this very benefit, that they are destinated to be grafted into him by faith, is to be fetched from him, and conferred on us in him. What therefore they say, that Christ has been predestinated Savior of the faithful only, that indeed is true, because he leads all the predestinated through to salvation only by faith; but not because faith is found in all the predestinated before the very decree of election.
pass_b: Christ the Church's Head is so joined to all his members that he holds causal priority over all the rest, and every outflow of free good to others comes through and for him — not only after they are grafted into Christ by faith, but so that even the benefit of being destinated to be grafted by faith is fetched from him and conferred on us in him. That Christ was predestinated Savior of the faithful only is true — he leads all the predestinated to salvation only by faith — not because faith is found in all the predestinated before the election decree itself.

lemmas.gloss: destined to be grafted by faith

title: Cap. V Obj. 6 Sol close: Arminius's foresight-election puts free will under election, not Christ
latin: Addo denique, si electio esset ex fide praevisa, ut philosophatur Arminius, id absurdi revera sequeretur, quod nobis conatur impingere. Nam posita lege tali, Quisquis credet, ad vitam eligetur, manifestum est homines ne proposito quidem Divino in Christo existentes, sed extra Christum omnimode consideratos, credendo mereri, aut saltem ex pacto consequi, electionem suam. Tali autem electioni liberum uniuscujusque arbitrium fundamenti loco potius substernitur, quam Christus, quando ab universali lege ad actualem particularem hominum electionem descenditur.
pass_a: I add finally, if election were from foresight faith, as Arminius philosophizes, that absurdity would in truth follow which he tries to fasten upon us. For such a law being posited, Whoever will believe will be elected to life, it is plain that men not even existing in the Divine purpose in Christ, but considered in every way outside Christ, by believing merit, or at least from a pact obtain, their election. But to such an election the free choice of each is rather laid under as a foundation, than Christ, when one descends from a universal law to the actual particular election of men.
pass_b: Finally: if election were from foresight faith as Arminius philosophizes, the absurdity he tries to pin on us would truly follow. Posit the law Whoever believes will be elected to life — then men not even existing in the divine purpose in Christ, but considered wholly outside Christ, by believing merit or at least by pact obtain their election. Under that election each one's free choice is laid as foundation rather than Christ, when one descends from a universal law to the actual particular election of men.
